question: Should OpenClaw approve a unified Settings i18n contract that includes schema/uiHint-derived config field labels, or keep the current work limited to UI chrome and quick-settings labels?
rationale: The existing source evidence shows simple UI chrome can use the current t() pipeline, but schema-derived labels come from config metadata and need a stable key/fallback contract before automation should implement the full request.

options.title: Approve Unified Settings I18n Contract
options.body: Route Settings chrome, quick settings, section metadata, and schema/uiHint labels through generated locale keys with English fallback, then refresh the partial PRs or replace them with focused slices.

options.title: Land Chrome Slices Only
options.body: Refresh and review the toolbar and quick-settings PRs while leaving schema-derived field labels English until a later API/product decision.

options.title: Defer Settings Localization
options.body: Keep the issue open as a known UX gap and avoid adding new locale key surface until the Control UI i18n roadmap is explicitly prioritized.

recommendation.title: Approve Unified Settings I18n Contract
recommendation.body: Route Settings chrome, quick settings, section metadata, and schema/uiHint labels through generated locale keys with English fallback, then refresh the partial PRs or replace them with focused slices.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a Control UI i18n pipeline/key-shape decision, with schema metadata input from Takhoffman's area.
